THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is directed against the judgment and award in MVC No.634/2018 dated 06.12.2018 by the learned IX Additional Small Causes Judge and Additional MACT, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Additional Small Causes Judge and Additional MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the appellant before this Court.

2. Brief facts of the case are as below:
The petitioner had approached the Tribunal stating that on 01.01.2018, while he was traveling in Maruthi Swift Car bearing registration No.KA-40-A-5188 near Ranebennur bypass, the driver of the said car drove the same in high speed and negligent manner and dashed to the bridge wall and caused the accident.
It was stated that the petitioner and other inmates of the car sustained injuries and he was shifted to OM Hospital, Ranebennur and thereafter, Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru.
The petitioner contended that he was an electrician earning Rs.24,000/- per month and due to the accidental NC: 2023:KHC:20912 injuries, there is permanent disability.
It was contended that he suffered fracture of shaft of left femur and had undergone surgery but even then, he had suffered permanent disability.

Therefore,
the petitioner claimed compensation from the owner and insurer of the car.
3. On issuance of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are the insurer and the owner of the car have appeared before the Tribunal.
They filed objections contending that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law.
respondent No.1 also contended that the terms and conditions of the policy was violated by the owner and driver and as such, the liability was denied.

The respondent No.2-owner contended that the driver had valid driving license and as such, the liability be fastened upon the respondent No.1.
4.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW.1, the Doctor who assessed his disability was examined as PW.2 and Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.
Neither any evidence was led nor any documents was produced by the Sri. Vinay Kumar vs M/S Universal Sompo on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117650782/

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal allowed the petition and awarded a sum of Rs.2,73,048/- as compensation to the petitioner and directed the respondent No.1 to pay the same under the following heads:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.) For pain and sufferings, 40,000/-
 mental agony  Actual medical expenses 14,248/-
 For special diet and  10,000/-
 conveyance  For loss of earning during  16,000/-
 treatment period  Permanent disability 1,72,800/-
 Future medical expenses 20,000/-
 TOTAL 2,73,048/-
 6.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal and contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate, low and meager.
7. On issuance of notice by this Court, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and notice to respondent No.2 was dispensed with.
The Tribunal records have been secured.
The arguments by both the sides are heard.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submit that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the notional income of the petitioner.
He contend that the compensation under the head of 'future medical expenses' and 'loss of earning during treatment period' need to be enhanced.
9. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1 submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is adequate and there is no need for enhancement.

10. The fact that there was an accident involving the car owned by the respondent No.2 insured by respondent No.1 and that it had met with an accident, while the petitioner was inmate of the said car is not in dispute.

The records reveal that the petitioner had sustained fracture of shaft of left femur and it was treated with nailing and Closed Reduction And Internal Fixation (for short 'CRIF') and he was inpatient for a period of 14 days.

The petitioner claims that he was an Electrician, aged 21 years Sri. Vinay Kumar vs M/S Universal Sompo on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117650782/
3 and he has sustained the disability.

sentences.text: PW.2 states that he assessed the disability and it was 32.8% of the left lower limb.
He assessed the whole body disability at 16.4%.
The Tribunal considering the fact that petitioner was an Electrician, NC: 2023:KHC:20912 held the functional disability to be 10%.
It is relevant to note that there are no reasons to vary the disability assessed by the Tribunal as the fracture was treated with nailing and CRIF.

11. The Tribunal held that in the absence of any cogent evidence regarding income of the petitioner,
the notional income of Rs.8,000/- has to be taken.
The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for settlement of disputes before Lok-Adalath prescribe notional income of RS.12,500/- for the year 2018.
In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, there is no reason not to accept the notional income of Rs.12,500/- per month.
Hence, the 'loss of income due to the disability' sustained is calculated as Rs.12,500/- X 12 X 18 X 10 % = 2,70,000/- by adopting multiplier of 18 for the age of 21 years.

12. As a consequence, the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during laid up period'
need to be revised for 2 months, the same is assessed at Rs.25,000/-.

13. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and suffering', 'medical expenses', 'special NC: 2023:KHC:20912 diet and conveyance' are adequate and do not require any enhancement.
The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner needs Rs.50,000/- for 'future medical expenses'.
However, he has not shown the assessment for the same.
Hence, the compensation under this head needs to be enhanced to RS.40,000/-.
Hence, the compensation is reassessed under different heads as below:

AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.) Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 Medical Expenses 14,248/-
 Special diet and conveyances 10,000/-
 Loss of income during laid up  25,000/-
 period

Loss of income due to  2,70,000/-
 disability  Future medical expenses 40,000/-
 TOTAL 3,99,248/-
 Less: awarded by the  Tribunal 2,73,048/-
 Enhancement 1,26,200/-

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for enhanced Sri. Vinay Kumar vs M/S Universal Sompo on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117650782/

Hence, the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:20912 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.1,26,200/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
(iii) The respondent No.1- Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Rest of the order of the Tribunal stands unaltered.
